text.paragraph: Establishing care: a high blood pressure reading at a boxing commission check, trauma-informed history, alcohol and drug screening with a safety assessment, and health literacy [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: He wants to keep fighting and needs his blood pressure under control to pass the commission physical. [S]
He wants things explained to him out loud, not handed to him on paper. [S]
He knows he drinks too much between fights and wants to cut down without being lectured. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Charles L. Liston was born in St. Francis County, Arkansas, to sharecroppers Tobe and Helen Liston. His birth date is uncertain: there was no birth certificate (Arkansas did not require them until 1965); he filed for one in 1953 giving May 8, 1932, which the Encyclopedia of Arkansas and the Scribner encyclopedia use with a question; his family's 1930 census record does not list him, so he was probably born no earlier than late 1930; his mother gave several dates; and other sources suggest 1927 or 1928. [D]

He was one of many children (the ninth of his mother's ten; one account counts twenty-two siblings and half-siblings), worked full-time in the cotton fields by the age of eight, and was beaten regularly by his father. [D]
He had virtually no schooling and never learned to read or write. [D]

At thirteen he followed his mother to St. Louis. Arrested in 1950 after a series of robberies, he was sentenced to five years in the Missouri State Penitentiary in Jefferson City, where a Catholic chaplain encouraged him to box; he was paroled in 1952. [D]

He turned professional in September 1953 and broke his jaw in a 1954 loss. He won the world heavyweight title in Chicago on September 25, 1962, with a first-round knockout, and lost it in Miami Beach on February 25, 1964, when he did not come out for the seventh round, citing a shoulder injury; he lost the rematch in 1965. His record was 50 wins (39 by knockout) and 4 losses; he moved to Las Vegas in 1966. [D]
He was described as a heavy drinker and a reckless driver with frequent arrests. [D]

text.paragraph: 4 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

list.item: Professional heavyweight boxer, still competing and training six days a week; married; lives in Las Vegas [S]
Grew up on a farm with many brothers and sisters; did field work from childhood and had almost no schooling; does not read or write and asks that forms and instructions be read to him [S]

Alcohol: vodka or beer most days, usually two or three drinks and five to six on weekend nights (about 25 drinks a week); has tried to cut down before training camps [S]
No opioid, stimulant, cannabis or sedative use, no injection drug use (DAST-10 0); does not smoke [S]
No firearms in the home [S]
Health literacy: answers "always" to needing help reading health materials; strong memory for spoken instructions and demonstrations [S]
Strengths and supports: discipline and daily training, physical strength, a sharp memory, his family, his trainer and gym, and the steadiness he says boxing gave him [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, watchful at first and then relaxed once he was told what each step of the visit would be; speaks briefly and to the point; mood "all right"; no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone; no psychotic symptoms; insight good about drinking before fights. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

Confirm the blood pressure out of the office with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring before any diagnosis or medicine; baseline metabolic panel, glucose, lipids, urine albumin, TSH and ECG. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Hypertension in Adults: Screening (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Cardiology consultation on the same day as the two-week visit: confirm and stage the hypertension, echocardiogram, choice of treatment, and fitness to compete. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Eligibility and Disqualification Recommendations for Competitive Athletes With Cardiovascular Abnormalities: Task Force 6: Hypertension (Black HR, et al.) (2015) [S]

Alcohol: nonjudgmental brief intervention with motivational interviewing; a drinking goal he sets himself; medicines (naltrexone, acamprosate or topiramate) explained; AUDIT-C at each follow-up and liver tests. Guideline: The Healthcare Professional's Core Resource on Alcohol (2026); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders (2021); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018) [S]

Safety plan given out loud and as a picture card, with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline saved in his phone as a voice contact; safety reviewed at every visit. Guideline: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024) [S]

Health literacy universal precautions at every visit: plain spoken explanations, one or two key points at a time, teach-back, a picture-based medicine and blood pressure card, consent forms read aloud with time for questions, phone and voice-message reminders instead of letters, and an adult literacy program offered without pressure. Guideline: AHRQ Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd Edition (2024) [S]

Trauma-informed care: an ACE-informed history in which he chooses what to share, explanation and permission before each part of the examination, a PTSD screen, and counseling offered. Guideline: Trauma-Informed Care in Behavioral Health Services (Treatment Improvement Protocol 57) (2014); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Management of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Acute Stress Disorder (2023) [S]

Drug use screening with the DAST-10; naloxone and overdose education if any opioid use is reported or suspected. Guideline: Unhealthy Drug Use: Screening (2020); Opioid Overdose Reversal Medications (2026) [S]

Cardiovascular risk and preventive care at the preventive visit: lipids, risk estimate, immunizations and one-time screenings. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression monographs (2026) [S]
